terms.p: The compiler using a bit pattern the payload can never hold, such as a null pointer, to stand for a variant, so the enum needs no separate tag and takes no extra space.
A bit pattern a type can never legally hold, which the compiler is free to reuse to mean something else, such as the empty case of an Option.

terms.x: a method that transforms without unpacking
terms.p: A small method that takes a value and a closure and hands back a new value of the same shape, letting you describe a transformation without writing out the match by hand.
The small set of names the standard library brings into scope in every file automatically, which is why Some, None, Ok and Err need no import.
Tony Hoare's name for adding a null reference to a language in 1965, so called because absence and presence share one type and the check is never forced.
